Paper Title: A Comparative Study of Nickel, Cobalt, and Iron Oxyhydroxide Anodes for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of NiOOH, CoOOH, and FeOOH films prepared with comparable numbers of metal sites.
Advantages: The use of thin films with comparable metal sites enabled a systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of each material and allowed for the observation of multiple HMF oxidation pathways.
Limitations: The performances on flat, thick films may not be as good as catalysts deposited on 3D substrates.
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH film on FTO, Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: A Comparative Study of Nickel, Cobalt, and Iron Oxyhydroxide Anodes for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of NiOOH, CoOOH, and FeOOH films prepared with comparable numbers of metal sites.
Advantages: The use of thin films with comparable metal sites enabled a systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of each material and allowed for the observation of multiple HMF oxidation pathways.
Limitations: The rate of Co(OH)2/CoOOH-mediated HMF oxidation was too slow to generate sufficient current density for constant potential HMF oxidation before competing water oxidation occurred.
Catalysts: Anode: CoOOH film on FTO, Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: A Comparative Study of Nickel, Cobalt, and Iron Oxyhydroxide Anodes for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of NiOOH, CoOOH, and FeOOH films prepared with comparable numbers of metal sites.
Advantages: The use of thin films with comparable metal sites enabled a systematic comparison of the intrinsic catalytic activity of each material and allowed for the observation of multiple HMF oxidation pathways.
Limitations: FeOOH did not exhibit any catalytic activity for HMF oxidation at potentials below the onset for water oxidation. The combination of a high overpotential requirement and the predominance of water oxidation makes the FE for HMF oxidation extremely low.
Catalysts: Anode: FeOOH film on FTO, Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: A dynamic Ni(OH)2-NiOOH/NiFeP heterojunction enabling high-performance E-upgrading of hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: In-situ surface reconstruction of NiFeP to form a dynamic Ni(OH)2-NiOOH/NiFeP heterojunction which acts as the active catalyst.
Advantages: The heterojunction presents extraordinary performance, producing FDCA with a high yield and Faradaic efficiency.
Limitations: Competitive Oxygen Evolution Reaction (OER) occurs, especially at high overpotentials or under mass transfer limitations, which lowers the Faradaic efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni(OH)2/NiFeP on Nickel Foam (NF); Cathode: Graphite rod

Journal Name: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Paper Title: A General Strategy for Decoupled Hydrogen Production from Water Splitting by Integrating Oxidative Biomass Valorization
Key Feature: Integrated HMF oxidation and hydrogen evolution using a bifunctional Ni3S2/NF catalyst, replacing OER.
Advantages: Avoids explosive H2/O2 mixture and ROS formation, yields high-value products at both electrodes, significantly reduces cell voltage (~200 mV) compared to water splitting, and maximizes energy conversion efficiency.
Catalysts: Working electrode: Ni3S2/NF, Counter electrode: carbon rod, Reference electrode: Ag/AgCl

Journal Name: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Paper Title: A General Strategy for Decoupled Hydrogen Production from Water Splitting by Integrating Oxidative Biomass Valorization
Key Feature: Integrated HMF oxidation and hydrogen evolution using a bifunctional Ni3S2/NF catalyst, replacing OER.
Advantages: Avoids explosive H2/O2 mixture and ROS formation, yields high-value products at both electrodes, significantly reduces cell voltage (~200 mV) compared to water splitting, and maximizes energy conversion efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3S2/NF, Cathode: Ni3S2/NF

Paper Title: A versatile single-copper-atom electrocatalyst for biomass valorization
Key Feature: Single copper atoms supported on nitrogen doped carbon nanosheets (Cu/NCNSs)
Advantages: High atom-utilization efficiency, unique electronic structure, afforded abundant active sites and significantly promoted the reactions compared to Cu nanoparticles.
Limitations: Limited activity for the oxidation of furfural (Fur), methanol (MA), and oxalic acid (OA).
Catalysts: Anode: Cu/NCNSs on glassy carbon, Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: A versatile single-copper-atom electrocatalyst for biomass valorization
Key Feature: Commercial Cu nanoparticles used as a benchmark catalyst
Limitations: Poor catalytic activity towards OER and HMFOR compared to the single-atom catalyst.
Catalysts: Anode: Commercial Cu nanoparticles on glassy carbon, Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Activity origin and alkalinity effect of electrocatalytic biomass oxidation on nickel nitride
Key Feature: High alkalinity electrolyte to favor oxidation of aldehyde groups.
Advantages: The strong alkali environment is conducive to the conversion of HMF due to the increased active species (Ni2+N(OH)ads) and the enhanced adsorption of HMF. The reaction pathway is preferable to the oxidation of aldehyde groups.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3N on carbon paper, Cathode: Graphite rod

Paper Title: An Overall Reaction Integrated with Highly Selective Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural and Efficient Hydrogen Evolution
Key Feature: Integration of anodic HMF oxidation to FDCA with cathodic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), replacing the conventional oxygen evolution reaction (OER).
Advantages: Simultaneously produces two value-added chemicals (FDCA and H2), effectively promotes hydrogen production, and reduces energy consumption compared to water electrolysis.
Catalysts: Anode: CoFe@NiFe LDH on Ni foam; Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Avoiding Pitfalls in Comparison of Activity and Selectivity of Solid Catalysts for Electrochemical HMF Oxidation
Key Feature: Free-standing, high surface area Cu-foam used directly as the anode, serving as a benchmark material.
Limitations: Spontaneous degradation of HMF via non-electrochemical side reactions and cathode-promoted degradation are key challenges addressed by the proposed protocol.
Catalysts: Anode: Cu-foam | Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Avoiding Pitfalls in Comparison of Activity and Selectivity of Solid Catalysts for Electrochemical HMF Oxidation
Key Feature: Phosphor-treated bimetallic oxide (CuCoO_P) powder catalyst immobilized on an inert boron-doped diamond (BDD) support.
Advantages: The boron-doped diamond (BDD) support is suggested as suitable due to good conductivity and low intrinsic catalytic activity.
Limitations: Spontaneous degradation of HMF via non-electrochemical side reactions and cathode-promoted degradation are key challenges addressed by the proposed protocol.
Catalysts: Anode: CuCoO_P on BDD | Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Avoiding Pitfalls in Comparison of Activity and Selectivity of Solid Catalysts for Electrochemical HMF Oxidation
Key Feature: Electrodeposited Ni catalyst immobilized on an inert boron-doped diamond (BDD) support.
Advantages: The boron-doped diamond (BDD) support is suggested as suitable due to good conductivity and low intrinsic catalytic activity.
Limitations: Spontaneous degradation of HMF via non-electrochemical side reactions and cathode-promoted degradation are key challenges addressed by the proposed protocol.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni on BDD | Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Bifunctional integrated electrode for high-efficient hydrogen production coupled with 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation
Key Feature: Bifunctional CoNiP nanosheet integrated electrode (CoNiP-NIE) for both HMFOR and HER.
Advantages: Delivers lower voltage (1.46 V at 20 mA cm-2) and higher H2 evolution rate (41.2 L h⁻¹ m⁻²) compared to water splitting. The integrated electrode structure is beneficial for mass diffusion and electron transfer.
Catalysts: Anode: CoNiP-NIE, Cathode: CoNiP-NIE

Paper Title: Bifunctional integrated electrode for high-efficient hydrogen production coupled with 5-hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation
Key Feature: CoNi-LDH nanosheet integrated electrode (CoNi-LDH-NIE), the precursor material used as a baseline.
Advantages: Not specified in paper (used as a baseline for comparison)
Limitations: FE and yield decrease sharply at potentials exceeding 1.60 V vs. RHE. Inferior HMFOR performance with higher potential and lower current density compared to CoNiP-NIE.
Catalysts: Anode: CoNi-LDH-NIE, Cathode: CoNi-LDH-NIE

Paper Title: Bimetallic sites and coordination effects: electronic structure engineering of NiCo-based sulfide for 5-hydroxymethylfurfural electrooxidation
Key Feature: Hierarchical NiCo-based sulfide (NiCo-S) nanosheets grown on nickel foam
Advantages: Rapid reaction kinetics and low onset potential (1.2 V vs. RHE)
Catalysts: Anode: NiCo-S/NF, Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: Biomass upgrading coupled with H2 production via a nonprecious and versatile Cu-doped nickel nanotube electrocatalyst
Key Feature: Bifunctional Cu-doped Ni nanotube (NiCu NTs) catalyst on nickel foam for coupled HMF oxidation and H2 evolution.
Advantages: The cell potential required to deliver a benchmark current density of 100 mA cm-2 is decreased by 350 mV compared to conventional water splitting. The catalyst demonstrates robust stability, high faradaic efficiency, and high FDCA yield, even at high HMF concentrations (100 mM).
Catalysts: Anode: Cu-doped Ni nanotubes (NiCu NTs) on Nickel Foam; Cathode: Platinum gauze

Paper Title: Biomass Valorization via Paired Electrosynthesis Over Vanadium Nitride-Based Electrocatalysts
Key Feature: Anodic oxidation (ECO) of HMF using 3D VN hollow nanosphere catalyst in a two-compartment cell.
Advantages: The 3D hollow nanosphere morphology provides low-resistance diffusion channels, facilitating diffusion and ion transport of the electrolyte.
Catalysts: Anode: VN/NiF, Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: Biomass Valorization via Paired Electrosynthesis Over Vanadium Nitride-Based Electrocatalysts
Key Feature: Anodic oxidation (ECO) in an integrated paired electrolysis system using a VN catalyst-coated bipolar membrane.
Advantages: Shortens electron transport pathway, maximizes electrocatalytic activity, reduces electrical energy consumption, and shows potential for large-scale biomass conversion.
Limitations: Requires downstream purification (e.g., preparative high performance liquid chromatography) to obtain high purity products.
Catalysts: Anode: VN, Cathode: Pd/VN (both coated on a bipolar membrane)
Potential_raw: Constant current of 100 mA (cell voltage 2.5-3.0 V)

Paper Title: Cobalt-metalloid alloys for electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural as an alternative anode reaction in lieu of oxygen evolution during water splitting
Key Feature: Two-compartment flow cell with an anion exchange membrane separating the anodic and cathodic compartments.
Advantages: HMF oxidation is thermodynamically more favorable than water oxidation, leading to improved energy efficiency for H2 production and producing a valuable product (FDCA) instead of O2. The catalyst films also suffer less deactivation compared to OER.
Limitations: HMF substrate is unstable and decomposes in the highly alkaline electrolyte (1 M KOH), which competes with the desired oxidation to FDCA.
Catalysts: Anode: CoB modified nickel foam; Cathode: nickel foam

Paper Title: Collaborative Electrochemical Oxidation of the Alcohol and Aldehyde Groups of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural by NiOOH and Cu(OH)2 for Superior 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid Production
Key Feature: A mixed NiOOH-Cu(OH)2 catalyst on a high-surface-area nanofoam support enabling synergistic and rapid oxidation of HMF to FDCA.
Advantages: Instantaneous conversion of HMF to FDCA with high yield and Faradaic efficiency at a lower potential (1.40 V vs RHE) compared to foam electrodes.
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH-coated Cu(OH)2 nanofoam (Cu(OH)2/NiOOH) | Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Collaborative Electrochemical Oxidation of the Alcohol and Aldehyde Groups of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural by NiOOH and Cu(OH)2 for Superior 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid Production
Key Feature: A two-electrode flow reactor enabling stable HMF oxidation at high concentrations (50 mM) by maintaining a constant pH.
Advantages: Provides a better reaction environment than the H-type cell, allowing for operation at high substrate concentrations and demonstrating high stability over multiple cycles.
Catalysts: Anode: Cu(OH)2/NiOOH nanofoam | Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Combined biomass valorization and hydrogen production in a photoelectrochemical cell
Key Feature: Electrochemical oxidation using a TEMPO mediator with a standard Au working electrode.
Advantages: Achieved high yield and Faradaic efficiency at ambient temperature and pressure in a mildly basic aqueous solution without consuming chemical oxidants or generating chemical waste.
Limitations: Direct oxidation of HMF on the Au surface is not particularly favoured over water oxidation without the mediator.
Catalysts: Anode: Au working electrode, Cathode: Platinum counter electrode
Electrolyte: 0.5 M borate buffer solution (pH 9.2) containing 5 mM HMF and 7.5 mM TEMPO

Paper Title: Combined biomass valorization and hydrogen production in a photoelectrochemical cell
Key Feature: Solar-driven HMF oxidation using an n-type nanoporous BiVO4 photoanode, coupled with H2 production at the cathode.
Advantages: Significantly reduces the applied potential necessary for TEMPO oxidation by ~700 mV compared to electrochemical oxidation, utilizing solar energy.
Limitations: It is possible that some of the photogenerated holes were used for water oxidation, which could lower the Faradaic efficiency for FDCA formation.
Catalysts: Anode: n-type nanoporous BiVO4 photoanode, Cathode: Pt counter electrode
Electrolyte: 0.5 M borate buffer solution (pH 9.2) containing 5 mM HMF and 7.5 mM TEMPO

Paper Title: Combined biomass valorization and hydrogen production in a photoelectrochemical cell
Key Feature: Electrochemical oxidation using an inexpensive, high-surface-area carbon-felt electrode instead of a precious metal.
Advantages: Eliminated the need for precious-metal catalysts, reduced the required overpotential by 170 mV compared to Au, and shortened the reaction time due to high surface area.
Limitations: The geometric area of the electrode was limited to 1 cm² due to the cell size, which limited the absolute conversion rate in this specific experimental setup.
Catalysts: Anode: Carbon-felt working electrode, Cathode: Platinum counter electrode
Electrolyte: 0.5 M borate buffer solution (pH 9.2) containing 5 mM HMF and 7.5 mM TEMPO

Paper Title: Constructing multifunctional ‘Nanoplatelet-on-Nanoarray’ electrocatalyst with unprecedented activity towards novel selective organic oxidation reactions to boost hydrogen production
Key Feature: 'Nanoplatelet-on-Nanoarray' catalyst architecture derived from the transformation of a bimetallic metal-organic framework (MOF).
Advantages: The unique nanostructure facilitates charge and mass transfer, and the transformation enriches the population of surface active sites, leading to unprecedented activity.
Catalysts: Anode: t-Ni1Co1-MOF on Ni foam; Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Continuous electrochemical oxidation of biomass derived 5-(hydroxymethyl)furfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Divided cell with an anion exchange membrane (Fumasep® FAA-3-PK-130).
Advantages: Prevents cathodic reduction of HMF and its oxidation products, which improves Faradaic efficiency compared to an undivided cell.
Limitations: Using a Ni wire electrode, full conversion was not achieved for HMF concentrations >10 mM due to low surface area and required extended conversion times (>24 h).
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH (wire), Cathode: Pt gauze
Electrolyte: 0.3 M NaClO4 with a phosphate buffer (pH 12)

Paper Title: Continuous electrochemical oxidation of biomass derived 5-(hydroxymethyl)furfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Scaled-up (100 cm²) batch reactor using a high surface area Ni/NiOOH foam anode with continuous pH control.
Advantages: High surface area foam electrode allows for conversion of high HMF concentrations, overcoming limitations of wire electrodes.
Limitations: Increasing HMF concentration resulted in lower yields towards FDCA due to accelerated degradation of HMF at alkaline pH.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni/NiOOH foam, Cathode: Perforated platinized titanium
Electrolyte: 0.1 M Na2SO4 with continuous addition of 10 M NaOH to maintain pH 12

Paper Title: Continuous electrochemical oxidation of biomass derived 5-(hydroxymethyl)furfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Continuous two-step galvanostatic electrolysis in an 800 cm² reactor with integrated product separation via pH-shift crystallization.
Advantages: Enables continuous production and separation of FDCA at industrially relevant concentrations.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni foam, Cathode: Stainless steel

Paper Title: Controllable and facile preparation of Co9S8–Ni3S2 heterostructures embedded with N,S,O-tri-doped carbon for electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Ternary Co9S8-Ni3S2@NSOC heterostructure with a unique hollow structure, synthesized via one-step pyrolysis of a deep eutectic solvent (DES).
Advantages: Excellent HMF electrooxidation performance with high conversion, selectivity, and Faradaic efficiency, owing to the unique hollow structure and ternary heterogeneous interface. The synthesis strategy is described as facile, cheap, green, and controllable.
Limitations: The HMF conversion, FDCA selectivity and FE of the electrode decreased slightly in the continuous 10 cycle test, which may be caused by the slight decrease of the catalyst during the reaction.
Catalysts: Anode: Co9S8-Ni3S2@NSOC on nickel foam (NF); Cathode: graphite rod

Journal Name: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Paper Title: Cooperative Rh-O5/Ni(Fe) Site for Efficient Biomass Upgrading Coupled with H₂ Production
Key Feature: Single-atom Rh on nanoporous mesh-type NiFe layered double hydroxides (Rh-SA/NiFe NMLDH) creating cooperative adsorption sites for HMF (on Rh) and OHads (on Ni).
Advantages: Creation of atomic-level cooperative adsorption sites for OHads and HMF molecules and enhanced surface electronic exchange-and-transfer capabilities, leading to top-level activity, ultralow onset potential, high FDCA Faradic efficiency, and excellent long-term stability.
Catalysts: Anode (working electrode): Rh-SA/NiFe NMLDH, Cathode (counter electrode): Pt plate
Potential_raw: 1.30 V vs. RHE at 50 mA cm⁻²

Journal Name: Journal of the American Chemical Society
Paper Title: Cooperative Rh-O5/Ni(Fe) Site for Efficient Biomass Upgrading Coupled with H₂ Production
Key Feature: Integrated HMFOR//HER system using the bifunctional Rh-SA/NiFe NMLDH catalyst for both anode and cathode.
Advantages: Significantly decreased cell voltages compared to OER//HER systems; outstanding catalytic stability over 100 hours of continuous operation.
Limitations: The overall electrolytic current density decreased over time, attributed to the continuous consumption of HMF reactant.
Catalysts: Anode: Rh-SA/NiFe NMLDH, Cathode: Rh-SA/NiFe NMLDH

Paper Title: Copper-Based Catalytic Anodes To Produce 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid, a Biomass-Derived Alternative to Terephthalic Acid
Key Feature: Nanocrystalline Cu foam (NCF) electrode prepared by electrodeposition.
Advantages: Possesses a higher surface area and more catalytically active Cu ions, achieving higher FE and yield in a shorter time. HMF conversion and FDCA production were nearly perfectly proportional to the charge passed with no significant accumulation of intermediates.
Catalysts: Anode: Nanocrystalline Cu foam (NCF), Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Copper-Based Catalytic Anodes To Produce 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid, a Biomass-Derived Alternative to Terephthalic Acid
Key Feature: Plain bulk Cu electrode with a dense and featureless surface morphology.
Advantages: Used as a baseline for comparison to the NCF electrode.
Limitations: Lower yield and Faradaic efficiency compared to NCF. Conversion and yield were not proportional to charge passed. A significant accumulation of FFCA was observed, indicating the conversion of FFCA to FDCA is the rate-determining step.
Catalysts: Anode: Plain bulk Cu electrode, Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Coupling efficient biomass upgrading with H2 production via bifunctional CuxS@NiCo-LDH core-shell nanoarray electrocatalysts
Key Feature: CuxS@NiCo-LDH core-shell nanoarray on copper foam as anode for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: High conductivity from CuxS core, modulated electronic structure of NiCo-LDH shell, and open nanoarray structure for enhanced mass transfer and active site exposure.
Limitations: Leaching of copper from the CuxS core under anodic conditions.
Catalysts: Anode: CuxS@Ni0.75Co0.25OmHn/CF, Cathode (Counter): Pt sheet

Paper Title: Coupling efficient biomass upgrading with H2 production via bifunctional CuxS@NiCo-LDH core-shell nanoarray electrocatalysts
Key Feature: Bifunctional system using CuxS@NiCo-LDH/CF as both anode (HMF oxidation) and cathode (HER) for simultaneous FDCA and H2 production.
Advantages: Low cell voltage (1.34 V for 10 mA/cm2) for co-generation, replacing sluggish OER with thermodynamically favorable HMF oxidation.
Limitations: Leaching of copper from the CuxS core at the anode.
Catalysts: Anode: CuxS@Ni0.75Co0.25OmHn/CF, Cathode: CuxS@Ni0.75Co0.25OmHn/CF

Paper Title: Critical Practices in Improving the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid in 0.1 M KOH
Key Feature: An anion exchange membrane (AEM) was used as the separator in a three-electrode system to transport OH- from the counter electrode to the working electrode, maintaining anolyte pH.
Advantages: The AEM can efficiently transport OH- generated at the counter electrode to the working electrode, which prevents a decrease in local pH and allows for high FDCA yields at higher HMF concentrations.
Catalysts: Working Electrode: NiO/CF (carbon felt)

Paper Title: Critical Practices in Improving the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid in 0.1 M KOH
Key Feature: A two-electrode flow cell with recycled anolyte and catholyte, used to investigate product crossover through the AEM and adsorption losses to system components.
Limitations: Adsorption of products by the electrolysis system and penetration of HMF and its products through the AEM from anolyte to catholyte lead to significant carbon loss and lower calculated yields.
Catalysts: Anode: NiO/CF (carbon felt)
Electrolyte: Anolyte: 0.1 M KOH + 10 mM HMF | Catholyte: 0.1 M KOH

Paper Title: Cu-Ni Bimetallic Hydroxide Catalyst for Efficient Electrochemical Conversion of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Cu-Ni bimetallic hydroxide catalyst (CuNi(OH)2/C)
Advantages: Synergistic effect from the bimetallic CuNi catalyst resulted in high HMF conversion (100%), FDCA yield (93.3%), and Faradaic efficiency (94.4%).
Catalysts: Anode: CuNi(OH)2/C, Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Deep eutectic solvent stabilised Co-P films for electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Co-P catalyst electrodeposited on copper foam using a deep eutectic solvent (DES).
Advantages: Remarkably increased performance, long-term stability, and high durability. The DES solvent is non-toxic, low-cost, biodegradable, and has good ionic conductivity.
Limitations: Slow leaching of phosphorus from the electrode surface occurs over repeated cycles before stabilizing.
Catalysts: Anode: Co-P on copper foam prepared in DES (Co-P_DES), Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Deep eutectic solvent stabilised Co-P films for electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Co-P catalyst electrodeposited on copper foam using water as the solvent (baseline comparison).
Advantages: Serves as a baseline for comparison.
Limitations: Lower durability, significant phosphorus leaching, and conversion of the Co-P surface to cobalt oxide/oxyhydroxide during the reaction, leading to lower yield and FE.
Catalysts: Anode: Co-P on copper foam prepared in water (Co-P_H2O), Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Dispersive non-noble metal phosphide embedded in alumina arrays derived from layered double hydroxide precursor toward efficient oxygen evolution reaction and biomass upgrading
Key Feature: Dispersive Ni2P nanoparticles embedded in 2D amorphous Al2O3 arrays on a 3D nickel foam (NF) support, derived from a layered double hydroxide (LDH) precursor.
Advantages: Unique 3D nano/micro-architecture, multi-porous structure, interconnected conductive skeleton, highly dispersive Ni2P active sites, and enhanced adsorption of active intermediates.
Catalysts: Anode: NiP-Al2O3/NF, Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: Doped Mn Enhanced NiS Electrooxidation Performance of HMF into FDCA at Industrial-Level Current Density
Key Feature: Mn-doped NiS nanosheets grown directly on 3D graphite felt (GF) as a self-supported, binder-free anode.
Advantages: The catalyst exhibits high selectivity (98.3%), yield (97.6%), faradaic efficiency (94.2%), robust stability (10 cycles), and a high FDCA production rate (4.56 g/h) at industrial-level current density.
Catalysts: Anode: Mn0.2NiS/GF | Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Doped Mn Enhanced NiS Electrooxidation Performance of HMF into FDCA at Industrial-Level Current Density
Key Feature: A scaled-up (10 cm²) Mn0.2NiS/GF anode was used in a flow system to reduce concentration polarization and enhance mass transfer for high-throughput production.
Advantages: Achieved a high FDCA production rate of 44.32 g/h and demonstrated excellent stability over five continuous electrolysis cycles at a large current (5 A).
Catalysts: Anode: Mn0.2NiS/GF (10 cm²) | Cathode: Not specified in paper

Paper Title: Efficient Alkaline-Free Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid using Electrochemically-Charged NixCo1-x(OH)2 as a Redox Mediator
Cell Type: Decoupled two-step system (undivided cell for charging)
Key Feature: A two-step decoupling strategy using a solid NiCo(OH)2 redox mediator, separating electrochemical charging in an alkaline electrolyte from chemical HMF oxidation in pure water.
Advantages: Operates without strong alkaline conditions, prevents HMF polymerization, enhances product purity, and eliminates the need for a membrane, thus reducing reaction costs.
Catalysts: Working electrode/redox mediator: Ni0.85Co0.15(OH)2 on carbon cloth (CC)
Electrolyte: Charging step: 1.0 M KOH | Oxidation step: Pure water

Paper Title: Efficient Alkaline-Free Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid using Electrochemically-Charged NixCo1-x(OH)2 as a Redox Mediator
Key Feature: Use of a catalyst slurry (α-Ni0.85Co0.15(OH)2 powder) as a flowable electrode to enable continuous operation and scalability.
Advantages: Enhanced mass transfer, larger active surface area, higher catalyst dosage, and improved scalability for practical applications.
Catalysts: Redox mediator: α-Ni0.85Co0.15(OH)2 powder slurry | Charging electrode: Carbon cloth (CC)
Electrolyte: Charging step: 1.0 M KOH | Oxidation step: Pure water

Paper Title: Efficient electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid using the facilely synthesized 3D porous WO3/Ni electrode
Key Feature: A 3D porous electrode fabricated by a one-step hydrothermal growth of WO3 nanorods on Ni foam, providing a high electrochemically active surface area.
Advantages: The system uses a noble-metal free catalyst, operates under ambient conditions (avoiding high temperature and pressure), and the 3D porous structure enhances ion and mass transport.
Catalysts: Anode: WO3/Ni-0.18 on Ni foam | Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Efficient Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Using Co-Doped Ni3S2 Catalyst: Promising for H₂ Production under Industrial-Level Current Density
Key Feature: Self-supported, binder-free Co-doped Ni3S2 nanosheets grown directly on 3D Ni foam (NF) substrate.
Advantages: Co-doping results in a dramatic increase of ECSA (electrochemical surface area), modulates the electronic properties of Ni3S2, and facilitates electron/charge transfer and mass transfer processes, promoting catalytic activity.
Limitations: HMF can degrade into unfavorable Humins in an alkaline electrolyte environment, especially at concentrations above 20 mM, which can lead to carbon imbalances and decreased Faradaic efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: Co0.4NiS@NF, Cathode: Pt electrode

Paper Title: Efficient electrooxidation of biomass-derived aldehydes over ultrathin NiV-layered double hydroxides films
Key Feature: Use of ultrathin (2.6 nm) Ni3V1-layered double hydroxides (LDHs) film as the electrocatalyst.
Advantages: Demonstrated general applicability with high conversion (83.4%) and selectivity (95.2%) for furan aldehydes.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3V1-LDHs film on Ni foil, Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Efficient H₂ Evolution Coupled with Oxidative Refining of Alcohols via A Hierarchically Porous Nickel Bifunctional Electrocatalyst
Key Feature: Bifunctional 3D hierarchically porous nickel (hp-Ni) catalyst for concurrent H₂ evolution and alcohol oxidation, replacing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER).
Advantages: Reduced voltage requirement (~220 mV less than water splitting), avoids explosive H₂/O₂ mixtures, no ROS formation, produces valuable products at both electrodes, high Faradaic efficiency, and operates under ambient conditions.
Catalysts: Working Electrode (Anode): hp-Ni on Ni foam, Counter Electrode (Cathode): Carbon rod

Paper Title: Electrocatalysis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural at cobalt based spinel catalysts with filamentous nanoarchitecture in alkaline media
Key Feature: Filamentous nanoarchitecture of NiCo2O4 grown directly on Ni foam via a hydrothermal method.
Advantages: High electrocatalytic efficiency and recyclability, non-precious metal-based, no redox mediator required.
Catalysts: Anode: NiCo2O4/Ni foam, Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Electrocatalysis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural at cobalt based spinel catalysts with filamentous nanoarchitecture in alkaline media
Key Feature: Filamentous nanoarchitecture of Co3O4 grown directly on Ni foam via a hydrothermal method (used for comparison).
Advantages: Non-precious metal-based, no redox mediator required.
Limitations: Lower HMF oxidation efficiency compared to NiCo2O4.
Catalysts: Anode: Co3O4/Ni foam, Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic Oxidation of 5-(Hydroxymethyl)furfural Using High-Surface-Area Nickel Boride
Key Feature: Divided cell with two compartments separated by a PEEK-reinforced anion exchange membrane, using a high-surface-area NiB catalyst on Ni foam.
Advantages: Highly efficient and selective oxidation, high faradaic efficiency (close to 100%), high yield (98.5%), uses a low-cost electrocatalyst, and minimizes HMF degradation in alkaline solution.
Catalysts: Anode: NiB-modified Ni foam (NF), Cathode: unmodified NF

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic Oxidation of 5-(Hydroxymethyl)furfural Using High-Surface-Area Nickel Boride
Key Feature: Electrochemical flow-through reactor using a high-surface-area nickel boride (NiBx) modified Ni foam anode.
Advantages: Highly efficient oxidation with high faradaic efficiency (close to 100%) and high yield (98.5%) using a low-cost, non-noble metal electrocatalyst.
Catalysts: Anode: NiBx-modified Ni foam, Cathode: unmodified Ni foam

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural into the Monomer 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid using Mesostructured Nickel Oxide
Key Feature: Mesostructured NiO catalyst derived by CMK-1 templating (NiO-CMK-1).
Advantages: Significantly enhanced selectivity towards FDCA, higher HMF conversion, higher current density, and almost three times higher Faradaic efficiency compared to bulk NiO.
Limitations: At longer reaction times, a higher FDCA selectivity might be hindered by the reaction equilibrium between FDCA and FFCA.
Catalysts: Anode: NiO-CMK-1 on glassy carbon, Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural into the Monomer 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid using Mesostructured Nickel Oxide
Key Feature: Commercial (bulk) NiO catalyst used as a baseline for comparison.
Advantages: Used as a baseline for comparison.
Limitations: Low FDCA selectivity (30%), low HMF conversion (≈50%), and low Faradaic efficiency (up to 25%).
Catalysts: Anode: Commercial NiO on glassy carbon, Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid on supported Au and Pd bimetallic nanoparticles
Key Feature: Anion-exchange membrane (AEM) electrolysis flow cell reactor used to determine potential-dependent product distribution.
Advantages: Bimetallic catalyst demonstrated higher HMF conversion and much greater selectivity towards FDCA than monometallic catalysts due to synergistic effects.
Limitations: HMF conversion rate and FDCA selectivity dropped drastically at 1.2 V vs. RHE due to the formation of inactive metal-oxide species.
Catalysts: Anode: Pd2Au1/C, Cathode: Pt/C

Paper Title: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid on supported Au and Pd bimetallic nanoparticles
Key Feature: Anion-exchange membrane (AEM) electrolysis flow cell reactor used to determine potential-dependent product distribution.
Advantages: Superior performance among tested catalysts, achieving 83% molar yield of FDCA at 0.9 V. Exhibits advantages of both single components with facile alcohol and aldehyde group oxidation.
Limitations: FDCA selectivity dropped at 1.2 V vs. RHE compared to 0.9 V.
Catalysts: Anode: Pd1Au2/C, Cathode: Pt/C

Paper Title: Electro-catalytic oxidation of HMF to FDCA over RuO2/MnO2/CNT catalysts in base-free solution
Key Feature: A CNT-supported ruthenium-manganese mixed oxide catalyst (RuO2/MnO2/CNT) was used for HMF oxidation in a base-free, initially neutral aqueous electrolyte.
Advantages: The use of a neutral electrolyte minimizes equipment corrosion and environmental pollution, and the product (FDCA) can be easily separated by cooling the electrolyte to room temperature, making the process more cost-effective.
Limitations: Faradaic efficiency and carbon balance decrease over the course of the reaction due to product polymerization into humins.
Catalysts: Anode: RuO2/MnO2/CNT on carbon cloth | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Electrochemical biomass upgrading on CoOOH nanosheets in a hybrid water electrolyzer
Key Feature: Hybrid water electrolyzer using in-situ synthesized CoOOH nanosheets on copper foam as the anode to couple HMF oxidation with hydrogen evolution.
Advantages: Achieves ~100% conversion, ~100% selectivity, and ~100% Faradaic efficiency for FDCA production at a low operating voltage (1.423 V), replacing the high-overpotential oxygen evolution reaction with a value-added process.
Catalysts: Anode: CoOOH on Cu foam, Cathode: Pt/C on carbon cloth

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on CeO2-Modified Co3O4 with Regulated Intermediate Adsorption and Promoted Charge Transfer
Key Feature: A core-shell heterointerface catalyst with Co3O4 nanowires as the core and CeO2 nanoparticles as the shell, supported on nickel foam (NF).
Advantages: The construction of the heterointerface facilitates the structural evolution of catalysts and charge transfer, regulates intermediate adsorption, and reduces the activation energy of the dehydrogenation step in 5-formyl-2-furancarboxylic acid (FFCA), promoting its oxidation to FDCA.
Catalysts: Anode: NF@Co3O4/CeO2 | Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on Nickel Nitride/Carbon Nanosheets: Reaction Pathway Determined by In Situ Sum Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectroscopy
Key Feature: Bifunctional catalyst (Ni3N@C) for coupled HMF oxidation and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).
Advantages: Increased energy conversion efficiency of the electrolyzer by replacing OER with HMF oxidation, and generation of value-added products at both electrodes (FDCA and H2).
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3N@C, Cathode: Ni3N@C

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on Nickel Nitride/Carbon Nanosheets: Reaction Pathway Determined by In Situ Sum Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectroscopy
Key Feature: Strongly coupled Ni3N/carbon nanosheets (Ni3N@C) as a bifunctional catalyst for HMF oxidation and HER.
Advantages: Increased energy conversion efficiency, generation of value-added products at both electrodes (FDCA and H2), and reduces electrolyzer overpotential by at least 240 mV compared to OER.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3N@C on Ni foam. Cathode: Pt foil (for three-electrode setup) or Ni3N@C (for dual-electrode setup).

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on Nickel Nitride/Carbon Nanosheets: Reaction Pathway Determined by In Situ Sum Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectroscopy
Key Feature: Strongly coupled Ni3N/carbon nanosheets (Ni3N@C) as a bifunctional catalyst for HMF oxidation and HER.
Advantages: Increased energy conversion efficiency, generation of value-added products at both electrodes (FDCA and H2), and reduces electrolyzer overpotential by at least 240 mV compared to OER.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3N@C on Ni foam. Cathode: Pt foil (for three-electrode setup) or Ni3N@C (for dual-electrode setup).

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on Nickel Nitride/Carbon Nanosheets: Reaction Pathway Determined by In Situ Sum Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectroscopy
Key Feature: Bifunctional Ni3N@C nanosheet catalyst for coupled HMF oxidation and hydrogen evolution.
Advantages: Increased energy conversion efficiency by replacing OER with HMF oxidation, generating value-added products at both electrodes (FDCA and H2), and using nonprecious metal nitrides.
Catalysts: Working Electrode (Anode): Ni3N@C on Ni foam

Paper Title: Electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural on ternary metal–organic framework nanoarrays: enhancement from electronic structure modulation
Key Feature: In situ hydrothermal growth of a ternary (Co, Ni, Fe) metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoarray directly on Ni foam, which serves as an integrated, binder-free electrode.
Advantages: The system's high performance is attributed to the unique 2D MOF microstructure, the in situ growth approach ensuring stability and contact, and the synergistic effect of the mixed metals modulating the electronic structure.
Catalysts: Anode: CoNiFe-MOFs/NF | Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural over a molybdenum sulfide modified nickel-based catalyst
Key Feature: A molybdenum sulfide modified nickel-based catalyst (Ni-MoSx/NF) grown on nickel foam, where high-valence Mo promotes the rapid conversion of Ni2+ to Ni3+.
Advantages: The catalyst exhibits a large electrochemically active surface area and excellent conductivity, leading to superior catalytic performance. HMF oxidation is also shown to have more dynamic advantages than water oxidation at low potential.
Limitations: The catalytic performance slightly reduces after the third cycle, which may be due to the loss of partial catalyst during the continuous washing and drying of the catalyst surface.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni-MoSx/NF | Cathode: Platinum wire

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid (FDCA) in Acidic Media Enabling Spontaneous FDCA Separation
Key Feature: HMF oxidation in acidic media (pH 1) using a MnOx anode, enabling spontaneous FDCA precipitation upon cooling.
Advantages: Spontaneous FDCA separation without pH adjustment, reducing cost and salt waste.
Limitations: Formation of maleic acid as a significant byproduct (21.9% yield), limiting the maximum FDCA yield.
Catalysts: Anode: MnOx on FTO; Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid catalyzed by bio-inspired NiMn layered double hydroxide
Key Feature: A bio-inspired NiMn layered double hydroxide (Ni1Mn5-LDH) catalyst grown on nickel foam, where Mn ions promote the conversion of Ni(II) to Ni(III) to generate the reactive NiOOH intermediate.
Advantages: The catalyst achieves high efficiency with a relatively low bias potential and minimal reaction time for HMF conversion to FDCA.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni1Mn5-LDH on Nickel Foam (NF)

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural with NiFe Layered Double Hydroxide (LDH) Nanosheet Catalysts
Key Feature: NiFe LDH nanosheets grown directly on carbon fiber paper as a binder-free anode, with a Nafion membrane separating the anode and cathode.
Advantages: Uses earth-abundant, inexpensive catalysts (NiFe LDH) under ambient conditions, achieving near-quantitative yield and high Faradaic efficiency. The HMF oxidation is kinetically more favorable than water oxidation, allowing for simultaneous H2 production.
Limitations: At HMF concentrations above 100 mM, crossover of HMF from the anode to the cathode becomes significant, requiring improved membranes for practical application.
Catalysts: Anode: NiFe LDH nanosheets on carbon fiber paper; Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of HMF via Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Hydride Transfer on NiOOH and the Impact of NiOOH Composition
Key Feature: Use of a flat, thin-film pristine NiOOH electrode to quantitatively deconvolute indirect (hydrogen atom transfer) and potential-dependent (hydride transfer) oxidation pathways for HMF.
Advantages: The use of a flat, thin electrode minimizes re-adsorption of intermediates, enabling a more accurate mechanistic study compared to high-surface-area porous electrodes.
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH film on FTO | Cathode: Pt
Potential_raw: 0.55 V vs. Ag/AgCl; 1.52 V vs. RHE

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of HMF via Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Hydride Transfer on NiOOH and the Impact of NiOOH Composition
Key Feature: Use of a Co-doped (31%) NiOOH film to investigate the effect of cathodically shifting the Ni(OH)2/NiOOH redox potential on HMF oxidation pathways.
Limitations: The paper concludes that Co incorporation hinders FFCA adsorption, slowing its oxidation, and the lower overall reaction rate leads to degradation of HMF and its intermediates over the longer electrolysis time.
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH film with 31% Co on FTO | Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Electrochemical Oxidation of HMF via Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Hydride Transfer on NiOOH and the Impact of NiOOH Composition
Key Feature: Use of a Ga-doped (6.7%) NiOOH film to investigate the effect of anodically shifting the Ni(OH)2/NiOOH redox potential on HMF oxidation pathways.
Catalysts: Anode: NiOOH film with 6.7% Ga on FTO | Cathode: Pt

Paper Title: Electrochemical upgrading of biomass-derived 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and furfural over oxygen vacancy-rich NiCoMn-layered double hydroxides nanosheets
Key Feature: Oxygen vacancy-rich ultrathin NiCoMn-LDHs nanosheets (1.15 nm thick) grown on Ni foam (NF) used as the anode.
Advantages: The ultrathin nanosheets provide a larger contact area and more oxygen vacancies; the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox cycle promotes biomass oxidation over water oxidation; the cooperative effect of Ni, Co, and Mn enhances performance; the stable LDH structure ensures high efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: NiCoMn(2:1)-LDHs/NF, Cathode: Pt-wire

Paper Title: Electrochemical valorization of HMF using Ni/Graphite electrodes
Key Feature: Use of five parallel Ni-electrodeposited pencil graphite rod (Ni/PGR) electrodes to increase the active surface area and reduce reaction time.
Advantages: The electrodes are cost-effective and easily prepared, achieving results comparable to more complex and costly electrode systems.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni electrodeposited on pencil graphite rods (Ni/PGR) | Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Electrochemically synthesized Ce-doped Cu-mesh catalyst with high activity and stability towards HMF to FDCA conversion
Key Feature: A cerium-doped copper mesh catalyst (Ec CM-Ce) synthesized via a modified chronopotentiometry method.
Advantages: High selectivity (99.2%), yield (96.4%), Faradaic efficiency (92.6%), and stability. The synthesis method is novel, cost-effective, and has potential for large-scale industrial applications.
Catalysts: Working Electrode: Ce-doped Cu-mesh (Ec CM-Ce)

Paper Title: Electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural by a catalyst containing copper nanoparticles and single copper atoms
Key Feature: Copper nanoparticles supported on carbon black (CuNPs/C) used as the anode catalyst.
Advantages: High HMF conversion (98.4%), high FDCA yield (98.3%), excellent cycle durability, and avoids complicated product separation.
Catalysts: Anode: CuNPs/C | Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural by a catalyst containing copper nanoparticles and single copper atoms
Key Feature: Single copper atoms and copper nanoparticles co-embedded in nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (CuNPs@Cu/NCNSs).
Advantages: Excellent selectivity for the production of FFCA.
Limitations: FFCA yield decreases at potentials higher than 1.42 V; does not achieve full conversion to a single product.
Catalysts: Anode: CuNPs@Cu/NCNSs | Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural by a catalyst containing copper nanoparticles and single copper atoms
Key Feature: Single copper atoms supported on nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (Cu/NCNSs).
Advantages: High selectivity towards FFCA.
Limitations: Some HMF degradation to humus was observed during prolonged electrolysis.
Catalysts: Anode: Cu/NCNSs | Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Engineering the Electronic Structure of NiFe Layered Double Hydroxide Nanosheet Array by Implanting Cationic Vacancies for Efficient Electrochemical Conversion of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: A self-standing carbon paper-supported NiFe layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheet array with implanted cationic vacancies (d-NiFe LDH/CP).
Advantages: The implanted cationic vacancies increase the number of active sites, lower the charge transfer resistance, and tailor the electronic structure of metal sites, improving electrocatalytic performance. The self-standing design avoids polymer binders.
Limitations: HMF can degrade in the strongly alkaline solution via the Cannizzaro reaction, which can impair overall efficiency if not converted quickly by the catalyst.
Catalysts: Anode: d-NiFe LDH/CP, Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Enhanced Adsorption Ability of CoS-Doped CuS for Promoting Electrochemical Oxidation of HMF
Key Feature: Doping CuS with CoS optimizes the surface electronic structure of the catalyst, enhancing its adsorption capabilities for HMF and OH-.
Advantages: The CoS-CuS catalyst exhibits a lower onset potential, higher current density, and substantially higher Faradaic efficiency for FDCA generation compared to pure CuS. It also demonstrates excellent cyclic stability.
Catalysts: Anode: CoS-CuS on Nickel Foam | Cathode: Platinum electrode

Paper Title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-HMF to FDCA using cobalt-doped nickel hydroxide: Broadening the potential window and improving efficiency
Key Feature: Co-doping of nickel hydroxide catalyst effectively lowers the oxidation onset potential and broadens the operating potential window for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: Co doping improves the structural stability of Ni(OH)2 materials, reducing dissolution and structural collapse during electrochemical reactions, which extends catalyst lifespan and maintains activity across a broader potential range.
Limitations: While this work successfully broadens the operational potential window for HMFOR, the achieved current densities remain below industrial benchmarks, highlighting a clear avenue for future catalyst development.
Catalysts: Anode: Co0.15Ni0.85(OH)2/NF | Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-HMF to FDCA using cobalt-doped nickel hydroxide: Broadening the potential window and improving efficiency
Key Feature: Exploratory experiment using Mn as a dopant for Ni-based HMF oxidation catalyst.
Limitations: The MnNi(OH)2@Mn2O3/NF electrode series exhibited less ideal electrocatalytic activity for HMFOR and showed high activity only at individual potentials.
Catalysts: Anode: MnNi(OH)2@Mn2O3/NF-1 | Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-HMF to FDCA using cobalt-doped nickel hydroxide: Broadening the potential window and improving efficiency
Key Feature: Exploratory experiment using Zn as a dopant for Ni-based HMF oxidation catalyst.
Advantages: The ZnNi(OH)2/NF electrode series demonstrated high current densities and activities during the reaction, indicating good performance.
Limitations: Doping with Zn reduces the overall electrocatalytic activity.
Catalysts: Anode: ZnNi(OH)2/NF-0.5 | Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-HMF to FDCA using cobalt-doped nickel hydroxide: Broadening the potential window and improving efficiency
Key Feature: Exploratory experiment using Cu as a dopant for Ni-based HMF oxidation catalyst, which demonstrated superior performance.
Advantages: The CuNi(OH)2/NF-0.5 electrode exhibited a similar active potential range to the Co-doped electrode and demonstrated superior FE and FDCA yield.
Limitations: Doping with Cu hinders the conversion of Ni(OH)2 to NiOOH.
Catalysts: Anode: CuNi(OH)2/NF-0.5 | Cathode: Pt mesh

Journal Name: Applied Catalysis B: Environment and Energy
Paper Title: Enhanced electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural over tailored nickel nanoparticle assembly
Key Feature: The catalyst consists of nickel nanoparticles self-assembled into an ordered nanoarray structure on carbon paper, which enhances electrocatalytic performance.
Advantages: The ordered nanoarray structure provides a larger electrochemically active surface area, facilitates mass transfer of reactive species, and promotes the formation of the catalytically active Ni(III) oxyhydroxide phase at a low overpotential.
Limitations: Increasing the HMF concentration might accelerate non-Faradaic processes, leading to the formation of undesired humin byproducts. Further studies are needed to suppress these side reactions in concentrated substrates.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni nanoparticles on carbon paper (Ni/CP-1.5) | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Enhancing Ni oxidation reconstruction in Ni3Fe nanoalloy for efficient Electro-Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Fe-doping in the Ni3Fe nanoalloy catalyst promotes in-situ reconstruction to form highly active Ni(O)OH species, which lowers the reaction barrier for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: The catalyst is prepared via a facile ball milling-pyrolysis strategy, enabling a green HMF oxidation process under ambient conditions with high efficiency and selectivity.
Limitations: The catalyst exhibits weaker HMF adsorption compared to control materials, resulting in slightly lower performance at low potentials or low HMF concentrations due to mass transfer limitations.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni3Fe@NC on Nickel Foam | Cathode: Graphite sheet

Paper Title: Enhancing the electrocatalytic activity of CoO for the oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural by introducing oxygen vacancies
Key Feature: Introduction of oxygen vacancies into CoO catalyst via Se doping, creating a CoO-CoSe2 composite.
Advantages: The introduction of rich oxygen vacancies enhanced the catalytic activity and the selectivity to FDCA by increasing the electrochemical surface area and reducing charge transfer resistance.
Catalysts: Anode: CoO-CoSe2 on Carbon Paper; Cathode: Platinum gauze

Paper Title: Faceted Branched Nickel Nanoparticles with Tunable Branch Length for High-Activity Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Biomass
Key Feature: Synthesis of uniform, faceted, Au-core/Ni-branched nanoparticles with tunable branch length (optimal at 155 nm) via a cubic-core hexagonal-branch mechanism.
Advantages: High catalytic activity for HMF oxidation, attributed to high surface area and increased exposure of active {1010} facets.
Catalysts: Anode: Au-core Ni-branched nanoparticles (155 nm branch length). Cathode: Not specified in paper.

Paper Title: Faceted Branched Nickel Nanoparticles with Tunable Branch Length for High-Activity Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Biomass
Key Feature: Nonfaceted, nonbranched amorphous Ni sphere nanoparticles used as a baseline for comparison.
Limitations: Lower activity (7.2x lower than 155 nm branched NP), higher charge transfer resistance, and higher overpotential for Ni2+ oxidation compared to branched nanoparticles.
Catalysts: Anode: Amorphous Ni sphere nanoparticles. Cathode: Not specified in paper.

Paper Title: Hierarchical Nickel-Cobalt-Based Transition Metal Oxide Catalysts for the Electrochemical Conversion of Biomass into Valuable Chemicals
Key Feature: Hierarchical NiCo2O4 nanowires grown vertically on 3D Ni foam (NF)
Advantages: Use of non-precious-metal catalysts; hierarchical nanowire structure provides high electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) and more exposed active sites.
Catalysts: Anode: NiCo2O4 on Ni foam, Cathode: carbon rod

Paper Title: Hierarchical NiSx/Ni2P nanotube arrays with abundant interfaces for efficient electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Hierarchical NiSx/Ni2P nanotube arrays with abundant interfaces synthesized via a sequential electrodeposition strategy.
Advantages: The synergistic effect between NiSx and Ni2P, good electronic/ionic conductivity, novel hollow structure for efficient diffusion paths, and abundant contact interfaces facilitate electron transfer and enhance electrochemical performance.
Catalysts: Anode: NiSx/Ni2P nanotube arrays on carbon cloth (SNP-2), Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Hierarchically nanostructured NiO-Co3O4 with rich interface defects for the electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: 3D hierarchical nanostructured NiO-Co3O4 catalyst with rich interface defects and cation vacancies grown on Ni foam.
Advantages: The interface effect created abundant cation vacancies, modulated the electronic properties of Co and Ni atoms, raised the oxidation state of Ni species, and resulted in superb HMF oxidation activities with a low onset potential.
Catalysts: Anode: NiO-Co3O4 on Ni foam, Cathode: carbon rods

Paper Title: Hierarchically nanostructured NiO-Co3O4 with rich interface defects for the electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Hierarchically nanostructured NiO-Co3O4 catalyst with rich interface defects and cation vacancies grown on Ni foam.
Advantages: The interface effect created abundant cation vacancies, modulated the electronic properties of Co and Ni atoms, raised the oxidation state of Ni species, and resulted in superb HMF oxidation activities with a low onset potential.
Catalysts: Anode: NiO-Co3O4 on Ni foam, Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: Highly Efficient Biomass Upgrading by a Ni-Cu Electrocatalyst Featuring Passivation of Water Oxidation Activity
Key Feature: Bimetallic Ni-Cu catalyst on Ni foam (NF) with passivated OER activity
Advantages: Passivates the competitive OER process, enabling FE and yield for FDCA to remain over 95% over a wide potential range (1.40 V to 1.55 V) and providing superior long-term stability.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni-Cu/NF; Cathode: Not specified in paper

Paper Title: Highly Efficient Biomass Upgrading by a Ni-Cu Electrocatalyst Featuring Passivation of Water Oxidation Activity
Key Feature: Bimetallic Ni-Fe catalyst on Ni foam (NF) used as a comparative system with high intrinsic OER activity.
Advantages: Used as a comparative system to demonstrate the effect of high OER activity, which is undesirable for HMF oxidation.
Limitations: Intrinsic superb OER activity is a primary competing reaction, leading to inferior FEs (dropping from 85.35% to 41.34%) and yields. Generated O2 bubbles can block active sites and induce catalyst detachment.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni-Fe/NF; Cathode: Not specified in paper

Paper Title: Highly efficient electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) by Cu regulated Co carbonate hydroxides boosting hydrogen evolution reaction
Key Feature: Hybrid nanostructure catalyst (Co₁Cu₁-CH) composed of 1D nanorods and 2D ultra-thin nanosheets.
Advantages: Largest ECSA and specific surface area, smallest Tafel slope and impedance among tested catalysts. Boosts H2 evolution rate significantly compared to water splitting.
Catalysts: Anode: Co₁Cu₁-CH on Carbon Cloth (CC); Cathode: Pt plate
Electrolyte: Anolyte: 1 M KOH with 10 mM HMF; Catholyte: 0.5 M H2SO4

Paper Title: Highly Efficient Electro-reforming of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural on Vertically Oriented Nickel Nanosheet/Carbon Hybrid Catalysts: Structure-Function Relationships
Key Feature: Vertically oriented Ni nanosheet forests anchored on carbon paper.
Advantages: High efficiency in electrooxidation of HMF to FDCA, >99% selectivity, low operating potential of 1.36 V vs RHE, and high stability.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni nanosheet/Carbon Paper (Ni(NS)/CP). Cathode: Not specified in paper.

Paper Title: HMF electrooxidation on robust nickel-foam catalysts: effect of pH on electrolysis performance
Key Feature: A robust, electrodeposited Ni-foam catalyst was used to systematically determine the optimal OH-/HMF reactant ratio for maximizing FDCA production.
Advantages: The optimized reactant ratio (2-4) maximizes the reaction rate while minimizing excess alkali use and unwanted HMF degradation, enabling more economically viable FDCA production.
Limitations: The pH decreases during prolonged electrolysis due to the formation of carboxylic acid products, requiring active pH control to maintain performance.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni-foam | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Identifying the Geometric Site Dependence of Spinel Oxides for the Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Cu2+ introduced to replace Co2+ in spinel oxide (CuCo2O4) to enhance exposure of octahedral Co3+ active sites.
Advantages: Shows a 4-fold enhancement for HMF oxidation relative to Co3O4, a record performance among Co-based catalysts, and outstanding electrochemical stability.
Catalysts: Working electrode: CuCo2O4 on Ni foam

Paper Title: Identifying the Geometric Site Dependence of Spinel Oxides for the Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Baseline Co-based spinel oxide (Co3O4) with both tetrahedral (Co2+) and octahedral (Co3+) sites.
Advantages: Higher catalytic activity than ZnCo2O4 and CoAl2O4, indicating both tetrahedral and octahedral sites contribute to overall activity.
Limitations: Significantly lower activity compared to the optimized CuCo2O4 catalyst.
Catalysts: Working electrode: Co3O4

Paper Title: Identifying the Geometric Site Dependence of Spinel Oxides for the Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Spinel oxide (ZnCo2O4) where tetrahedral sites are blocked by Zn2+ to isolate the effect of octahedral sites.
Advantages: Used to mechanistically probe the role of different geometric sites in HMF oxidation.
Limitations: Inferior chemical adsorption ability and lower reaction kinetic rate compared to Co3O4.
Catalysts: Working electrode: ZnCo2O4

Paper Title: Improved Performance of Nickel Boride by Phosphorus Doping as an Efficient Electrocatalyst for the Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Phosphorus-doped nickel boride (NiBx-P0.07) catalyst on carbon paper used as the working electrode.
Advantages: Phosphorus doping accelerated charge transmission capability, modified the surface electronic structure, and increased surface nickel hydroxide species, which improved electrocatalytic activity for HMF oxidation.
Catalysts: Anode: NiBx-P0.07 on carbon paper; Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Integrated Catalytic Sites for Highly Efficient Electrochemical Oxidation of the Aldehyde and Hydroxyl Groups in 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Spinel oxide catalyst (Ni0.5Co2.5O4) with Ni introduced into tetrahedral sites to improve hydroxyl group oxidation activity.
Advantages: The integrated catalytic sites enhanced the overall activity of HMFOR, achieving high yield and faradaic efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni0.5Co2.5O4

Paper Title: Integrated Catalytic Sites for Highly Efficient Electrochemical Oxidation of the Aldehyde and Hydroxyl Groups in 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Baseline Co3O4 catalyst used for mechanistic investigation of direct and indirect HMF oxidation pathways.
Advantages: Allowed for identification of direct and synergistic oxidation types and revealed higher activity for aldehyde group oxidation over hydroxyl group oxidation.
Limitations: Higher reaction barrier for hydroxyl oxidation compared to aldehyde oxidation, leading to imbalanced reactivity.
Catalysts: Anode: Co3O4

Paper Title: Integrating Electrocatalytic 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation and Hydrogen Production via Co-P-Derived Electrocatalysts
Key Feature: HMF oxidation on an earth-abundant Co-P catalyst as an alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction.
Advantages: Uses earth-abundant electrocatalysts, is more thermodynamically and kinetically facile than OER, and produces a valuable product (FDCA).
Limitations: Post-electrolysis analysis showed the phosphorus amount in the catalyst was largely diminished, suggesting potential instability.
Catalysts: Anode: Co-P on copper foam (Co-P/CF)

Paper Title: Integrating Electrocatalytic 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation and Hydrogen Production via Co-P-Derived Electrocatalysts
Key Feature: Integrated HMF oxidation to FDCA and H2 production in a single electrolyzer using a symmetric Co-P/Co-P catalyst couple.
Advantages: Higher energy conversion efficiency than water splitting; required potential to reach 20 mA/cm² was 150 mV lower than for overall water splitting.
Catalysts: Anode: Co-P/CF, Cathode: Co-P/CF

Paper Title: Interfacial Engineering of MoO2-FeP Heterojunction for Highly Efficient Hydrogen Evolution Coupled with Biomass Electrooxidation
Key Feature: Porous nanospindle composed of carbon-encapsulated MoO2-FeP heterojunction (MoO2-FeP@C) as a bifunctional electrocatalyst.
Advantages: Interfacial electron redistribution enhances both HER and BEOR activity. The porous structure enlarges the accessible surface area. The bifunctional nature simplifies the system and reduces cost.
Catalysts: Anode: MoO2-FeP@C, Cathode: MoO2-FeP@C

Paper Title: Ni3N-V2O3 enables highly efficient 5-(Hydroxymethyl) furfural oxidation enabling membrane free hydrogen production
Key Feature: Bifunctional Ni3N-V2O3 catalyst used for both anode (HmfOR) and cathode (HER) in a symmetric, membrane-free configuration.
Advantages: Avoids the use of a membrane/diaphragm, avoids the need for intensive gas separation, and the cathode has strong tolerance to HMF.
Catalysts: Anode and Cathode: Ni3N-V2O3/NF (bifunctional)

Paper Title: Nickel(II)-modified covalent-organic framework film for electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF)
Key Feature: Use of a Nickel(II)-modified covalent-organic framework (COF) film (TpBpy-Ni@FTO) as a heterogeneous electrocatalyst.
Advantages: Highly porous structure allows for efficient diffusion of reactants and products; good thermal and chemical stability.
Limitations: The FDCA yield is not ideal (58%); low electroactive Ni coverage (5 ± 2)%; the final oxidation step (FFCA to FDCA) is the rate-determining step.
Catalysts: Anode: TpBpy-Ni@FTO (Nickel(II)-modified covalent-organic framework on fluorine-doped tin oxide)

Paper Title: NiSe@NiOx core-shell nanowires as a non-precious electrocatalyst for upgrading 5-hydroxymethylfurfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Three-electrode system with a NiSe@NiOx core-shell nanowire working electrode on nickel foam, separated by a N117 membrane.
Advantages: The core-shell structure provides abundant active sites (NiOx shell) and high electron transfer ability (NiSe core), leading to a small Tafel slope (23 mV dec-1), high yield, and robust stability.
Catalysts: Anode: NiSe@NiOx/NF, Cathode: Carbon rod

Paper Title: NiSe@NiOx core-shell nanowires as a non-precious electrocatalyst for upgrading 5-hydroxymethylfurfural into 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: Integrated electrolyzer using the NiSe@NiOx/NF catalyst bifunctionally as both anode and cathode for simultaneous HMF oxidation to FDCA and hydrogen (H2) evolution.
Advantages: Enables simultaneous production of value-added FDCA and H2 fuel. Requires a lower cell voltage (1.56 V for 20 mA/cm²) compared to overall water splitting (1.64 V).
Catalysts: Anode: NiSe@NiOx/NF, Cathode: NiSe@NiOx/NF

Paper Title: NiSx/carbon black hybrids for efficient electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethyfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: A hybrid catalyst (NiSx/CB-2) where an optimal amount of carbon black is doped into and encapsulates NiSx nanosheets, enhancing conductivity and active site exposure.
Advantages: The carbon black doping enhanced catalyst conductivity, increased specific surface area by separating nanosheets, facilitated charge transfer through C-S bond formation, and strengthened HMF adsorption capacity.
Limitations: The catalyst showed a decrease in activity after five cycles, attributed to the loss of Ni, structural fracturing of the catalyst, increased oxidation, and weakening of the interaction between carbon black and NiSx.
Catalysts: Anode: NiSx/CB-2 on Nickel Foam (NF) | Cathode: Graphite rod

Paper Title: Nitrogen modulated NiMoO4 with enhanced activity for the electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid
Key Feature: A nitrogen-modulated NiMoO4 nanoarray grown on Ni foam (N-NiMoO4/NF) was used as the anode catalyst.
Advantages: N-NiMoO4 has a higher electrochemical surface area and lower charge transfer resistance compared to un-nitrided NiMoO4, which enhances the activity and selectivity of the catalyst.
Limitations: The catalyst showed decreased activity after multiple cycles, with the FDCA yield dropping below 80% after the fourth cycle, attributed to a decrease in crystallinity and nitrogen content.
Catalysts: Anode: N-NiMoO4/NF | Cathode: Not specified in paper (Graphite rod used as counter electrode)

Paper Title: Nitrogen-doped Co3O4 nanowires enable high-efficiency electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Nitrogen doping of Co3O4 nanowires grown on nickel foam creates defects (N-dopants, oxygen vacancies) that enhance catalytic activity for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: The catalyst is cost-effective and exhibits superior HMF oxidation catalytic activity, durability, and structural stability compared to the undoped material.
Catalysts: Anode: Nitrogen-doped Co3O4 nanowires on Nickel Foam (N-Co3O4/NF-2) | Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: NiV Layered Double Hydroxide for Efficient and Scalable Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to High-Purity 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: NiV Layered Double Hydroxide (LDH) catalyst with V incorporation to stabilize the Ni³⁺ active state and promote HMF adsorption.
Advantages: Achieved high FDCA yields (>95%) at a low potential (1.35 V vs RHE) by accelerating the oxidation of the rate-determining intermediate, FFCA.
Limitations: The batch reaction setup is prone to base-induced degradation of HMF and its derivatives, which reduces FDCA yield and purity, especially at higher concentrations or longer reaction times.
Catalysts: Working electrode: NiV LDH on Ni foam

Paper Title: NiV Layered Double Hydroxide for Efficient and Scalable Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to High-Purity 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid
Key Feature: Spatially separates the pH-neutral HMF feed from the alkaline electrolyte, which are mixed just before entering the reactor to minimize base-induced degradation.
Advantages: Enables continuous production of high-purity FDCA (97.2%) at a high rate (62 g/day) by minimizing side reactions and maintaining stable operation over 40 h.
Catalysts: Anode: NiV LDH | Cathode: NiMo
Electrolyte: 1 M KOH with 0.5 M KHCO3 (mixed with 0.1 M HMF solution)

Paper Title: Operando Forming of Lattice Vacancy Defect in Ultrathin Crumpled NiVW-Layered Metal Hydroxides Nanosheets for Valorization of Biomass
Key Feature: Crumpled ternary NiVW-layered metal hydroxide (LMH) nanosheets with abundant lattice vacancies formed operando.
Advantages: High current density (193 mA cm-2 at 1.43 V vs RHE), exposes more unsaturated Ni activity sites, improves electrochemical active surface area, and promotes charge transfer, leading to high conversion and selectivity.
Catalysts: Anode: NiVWv-LMH grown on nickel foam (NF), Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Oxidation of biomass derived 5-hydroxymethylfurfural using heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis
Key Feature: Electrocatalytic oxidation on a Pt foil electrode at a constant current density, eliminating the need for molecular oxygen.
Advantages: Provides electrode potential and faradaic current as additional external control parameters; eliminates the use of molecular oxygen by in situ generation of reactive oxygenated surface species from the aqueous solvent.
Limitations: The product distribution is different from the heterogeneously catalyzed process, with high selectivity towards FDC instead of FDCA.
Catalysts: Anode: Pt foil, Cathode: Pt gauze
Electrolyte: pH 10 aqueous solution with 0.3 M NaClO4

Paper Title: Oxidation of biomass derived 5-hydroxymethylfurfural using heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis
Key Feature: Thermally activated, pressurized liquid-phase oxidation using molecular oxygen.
Catalysts: Au/TiO2

Paper Title: Platinum Modulates Redox Properties and 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Adsorption Kinetics of Ni(OH)2 for Biomass Upgrading
Key Feature: Pt nanoparticles loaded on Ni(OH)2 nanosheets to form a heterostructure catalyst.
Advantages: The introduction of Pt optimizes the redox property of Ni(OH)2, accelerates the formation of the active Ni(OH)O species, reduces the adsorption energy of HMF, and improves the current density for HMFOR by 8.2 times compared to bare Ni(OH)2.
Catalysts: Anode: Pt/Ni(OH)2

Paper Title: Promotion and Stabilization of High-Valence CoO2 for the Efficient Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) toward 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid (FDCA)
Key Feature: A Co(OH)2/Cu(OH)2 heterostructure on copper foam where electronic transfer from Co to Cu facilitates the generation and stabilization of high-valence CoO2 active sites.
Advantages: Effectively alleviates HMF degradation, achieves a carbon balance approaching 100%, and enhances reaction efficiency and stability for FDCA production.
Catalysts: Anode: Co(OH)2/Cu(OH)2 on Copper Foam (CF) | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Promotion and Stabilization of High-Valence CoO2 for the Efficient Electrooxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) toward 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid (FDCA)
Key Feature: Co(OH)2 nanosheets directly electrodeposited on copper foam, serving as a baseline catalyst for comparison.
Limitations: Insufficient generation and easy reduction of CoO2 active sites at high potentials, leading to low current density, poor FDCA productivity, and significant HMF degradation.
Catalysts: Anode: Co(OH)2 on Copper Foam (CF) | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Realizing efficient electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural on a freestanding Ni(OH)2/nickel foam catalyst
Key Feature: A freestanding Ni(OH)2/NF catalyst was fabricated via a facile in-situ acid-corrosion-induced strategy, creating a compact interface between the active material and the support.
Advantages: The in-situ formation strategy results in a compact interface between Ni(OH)2 and Ni foam, which contributes to good conductivity and stability during electrochemical reactions.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni(OH)2/NF | Cathode: Pt sheet

Paper Title: Realizing efficient electrochemical oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural on a freestanding Ni(OH)2/nickel foam catalyst
Key Feature: A scaled-up device using the freestanding Ni(OH)2/NF catalyst in a continuous-flow electrolytic cell to achieve a high FDCA production rate.
Advantages: The system overcomes mass transport limitations, exhibits superior mass transfer characteristics, and shows good stability for more than 60 h of operation.
Limitations: Performance decreased slightly after 30 hours of high-speed washing.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni(OH)2/NF | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Refining d-band center in Ni0.85Se by Mo doping: A strategy for boosting hydrogen generation via coupling electrocatalytic oxidation 5-hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Bifunctional NF@Mo-Ni0.85Se catalyst used for both anode and cathode in a symmetric two-electrode configuration for coupled HMF oxidation and hydrogen production.
Advantages: Requires a lower potential of 1.50 V to reach 50 mA cm-2 compared to overall water splitting (1.68 V), indicating higher energy efficiency. The kinetics of biomass electrooxidation are more favorable than that of OER.
Catalysts: Anode: NF@Mo-Ni0.85Se, Cathode: NF@Mo-Ni0.85Se

Paper Title: Selective Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Biomass-Derived 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-Diformylfuran: from Mechanistic Investigations to Catalyst Recovery
Key Feature: Use of cost-effective and sustainable non-precious metal electrodes (graphite anode, stainless-steel cathode) and focus on catalyst recovery via nanofiltration.
Advantages: Environmentally friendly process using cost-effective and sustainable electrodes, eliminating the need for precious metals. Achieves excellent selectivity, good yield, and excellent catalyst recovery.
Limitations: The paper notes the difficulty in recovering native TEMPO and the slower reaction rates of heterogeneous TEMPO derivatives, which prompted the design of a new size-enlarged catalyst for efficient recovery.
Catalysts: Anode: Graphite, Cathode: Stainless steel, Mediator: TEMPO
Electrolyte: 0.1 M LiClO4 in MeCN with 2,6-lutidine (1.0 equiv)

Paper Title: Selective Electrooxidation of Biomass-Derived Alcohols to Aldehydes in a Neutral Medium: Promoted Water Dissociation over a Nickel-Oxide-Supported Ruthenium Single-Atom Catalyst
Key Feature: Comparative experiment using the Ru₁-NiO catalyst in an alkaline electrolyte (KOH) for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: Facilitates higher HMFOR activity (3.2 times higher current density at 1.5 V) compared to the neutral medium.
Limitations: Low selectivity towards the aldehyde (DFF) product; favors over-oxidation to the carboxylic acid (FDCA).
Catalysts: Anode: Ru₁-NiO, Cathode: Graphite rod

Paper Title: Simultaneous H₂ Generation and Biomass Upgrading in Water by an Efficient Noble-Metal-Free Bifunctional Electrocatalyst
Key Feature: A bifunctional electrocatalyst (Ni₂P NPA/NF) was used for both the anode (HMF oxidation) and cathode (H₂ evolution) in a coupled system.
Advantages: Replacing the sluggish OER with a thermodynamically more favorable biomass oxidation reaction generates value-added products at both electrodes (H₂ and FDCA) and increases the energy conversion efficiency by lowering the required cell voltage.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni₂P nanoparticle arrays on nickel foam (Ni₂P NPA/NF), Cathode: Ni₂P NPA/NF

Paper Title: Single-atoms Ru/NiFe layered double hydroxide electrocatalyst: Efficient for oxidation of selective oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and oxygen evolution reaction
Key Feature: Single Ru atoms supported on NiFe layered double hydroxide (LDH) synthesized via a two-step electrodeposition method.
Advantages: Exhibits excellent HMF conversion (99.43%), FDCA selectivity (99.24%) and yield (98.68%) at room temperature.
Catalysts: Anode: Ru0.3/NiFe LDH on Nickel Foam (NF); Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Stabilities, Regeneration Pathways, and Electrocatalytic Properties of Nitroxyl Radicals for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: TEMPO-mediated homogeneous electrocatalysis for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: Can efficiently achieve HMF oxidation in mildly basic conditions (pH 9-10), avoiding humin formation which is common with heterogeneous catalysts in strongly basic media.
Limitations: TEMPO evaporates at elevated temperatures (e.g., 40°C), requiring a sealed cell to prevent catalyst loss.
Catalysts: Anode: Carbon felt, Cathode: Pt, Mediator: 8 mM TEMPO

Paper Title: Stabilities, Regeneration Pathways, and Electrocatalytic Properties of Nitroxyl Radicals for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: ACT-mediated homogeneous electrocatalysis, using a less expensive TEMPO derivative.
Advantages: ACT is a more cost-effective catalyst than TEMPO and has a much lower vapor pressure, making it more stable against evaporation at elevated temperatures (40°C).
Limitations: The oxidized form, ACT+, is less stable than TEMPO+ at pH > 10. It also requires a more positive potential to be generated compared to TEMPO.
Catalysts: Anode: Carbon felt, Cathode: Pt, Mediator: 8 mM 4-acetamido-TEMPO (ACT)

Paper Title: Stabilities, Regeneration Pathways, and Electrocatalytic Properties of Nitroxyl Radicals for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: High concentration (100 mM HMF) oxidation using ACT mediator to demonstrate viability for large-scale production.
Advantages: Achieved a high initial current density (>200 mA/cm^2), which is critical for commercial viability. The use of a mediator alleviates mass transport limitations of the final oxidation step.
Limitations: Physical loss of product (FDCA) and intermediates due to trapping in the porous electrode, membrane adsorption, and crossover to the cathode compartment.
Catalysts: Anode: Carbon felt, Cathode: Pt, Mediator: 40 mM 4-acetamido-TEMPO (ACT)

Paper Title: Stabilities, Regeneration Pathways, and Electrocatalytic Properties of Nitroxyl Radicals for the Electrochemical Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: High concentration HMF oxidation at elevated temperature (40°C) to improve reaction kinetics.
Advantages: Operating at 40°C significantly decreased the reaction time while maintaining high HMF conversion and achieving a higher FDCA yield (95.9%) compared to room temperature.
Limitations: The oxidized mediator, ACT+, becomes unstable if the temperature is raised further to 60°C.
Catalysts: Anode: Carbon felt, Cathode: Pt, Mediator: 40 mM 4-acetamido-TEMPO (ACT)

Paper Title: Stabilization of alkaline 5-HMF electrolytes via Cannizzaro reaction for the electrochemical oxidation to FDCA
Key Feature: Pre-conversion of HMF into stable Cannizzaro products (DHMF and HMFCA) in highly alkaline media prior to electro-oxidation, enabling the use of high substrate and base concentrations.
Advantages: Allows for electro-oxidation at elevated concentrations of base (5 M) and HMF (0.25 M) while avoiding rapid degradation into humins, improving the atom economy and achieving high current densities (>1 A/cm²).
Limitations: The overall yield (~80%) is mainly limited by the incomplete chemical conversion of HMF to the stable Cannizzaro products prior to electrolysis.
Catalysts: Anode: Fe-modified Ni-foam (NiFe-layer double hydroxide/FeOOH heterostructures)
