Paper Title: Strain-induced in situ formation of NiOOH species on Co—Co bond for selective electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and efficient hydrogen production
Key Feature: Strain-induced in situ formation of NiOOH active species on a NiCo2O4 catalyst, enabled by the Co-Co bond strain, for coupled HMF oxidation and hydrogen production.
Advantages: Replaces sluggish water oxidation with thermodynamically favorable HMF oxidation, achieves high selectivity (>99%) and Faradaic efficiency (>99%) for FDCA production, and enhances hydrogen production by 8.16 times compared to water splitting.
Catalysts: Anode: NiCo2O4 nanowire on nickel foam (NF), Cathode: Platinum foil

Paper Title: Strongly Coupled 3D N-Doped MoO2/Ni3S2 Hybrid for High Current Density Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis and Biomass Upgrading
Key Feature: Bifunctional catalyst (N-MoO2/Ni3S2 NF) used as the working electrode for anodic HMF oxidation.
Advantages: HMF oxidation is energetically more favorable than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), enabling energy-efficient hydrogen production when coupled.
Catalysts: Anode: N-MoO2/Ni3S2 NF on Ni foam

Paper Title: Strongly Coupled 3D N-Doped MoO2/Ni3S2 Hybrid for High Current Density Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis and Biomass Upgrading
Key Feature: Symmetric cell using the same bifunctional catalyst (N-MoO2/Ni3S2 NF) as both anode and cathode for simultaneous HMF oxidation and hydrogen evolution.
Advantages: Requires a lower cell voltage (2.08 V) to achieve 100 mA cm-2 compared to overall water splitting (2.25 V), enhancing energy efficiency.
Catalysts: Anode: N-MoO2/Ni3S2 NF, Cathode: N-MoO2/Ni3S2 NF

Paper Title: Substrate molecule adsorption energy: An activity descriptor for electrochemical oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF)
Key Feature: Co-doping of NiO grown on carbon cloth (CC) to tune the HMF adsorption energy, thereby optimizing catalytic activity for HMF oxidation.
Advantages: The optimized 3%Co-NiO/CC catalyst shows high catalytic activity, yield, and Faradaic efficiency, exceeding most reported transition metal oxide (TMO) catalysts, along with robust electrochemical stability.
Catalysts: Anode: 3%Co-NiO/CC | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Tailorable Electrocatalytic 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation and H2 Production: Architecture-Performance Relationship in Bifunctional Multilayer Electrodes
Key Feature: Layer-by-layer (LbL) assembled fully alternating Au and Pd nanoparticles ((AuPd)7) on an ITO working electrode.
Advantages: Exhibited the highest current density for HMF oxidation (3.24 mA/cm²), a 225% improvement compared to the monometallic Pd14 electrode.
Limitations: Electrocatalytic performance decreases after a critical thickness is reached due to mass transfer limitations of HMF into the 3D electrode structure.
Catalysts: Working Electrode: (AuPd)7 on ITO-coated glass; Counter Electrode: Pt wire; Reference Electrode: Hg/HgO

Paper Title: Tailorable Electrocatalytic 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation and H2 Production: Architecture-Performance Relationship in Bifunctional Multilayer Electrodes
Key Feature: Asymmetric cell with independently optimized LbL electrodes: Pd7/Au7 anode for HMF oxidation and (AuPd)7 cathode for HER.
Advantages: Optimized full-cell system combining the best anode for HMF oxidation and the best cathode for HER, leading to improved overall performance compared to symmetric cell configurations.
Catalysts: Anode: Pd7/Au7 on ITO; Cathode: (AuPd)7 on ITO

Paper Title: Tailoring Competitive Adsorption Sites by Oxygen-Vacancy on Cobalt Oxides to Enhance the Electrooxidation of Biomass
Key Feature: Oxygen-vacancy rich Co3O4 (Vo-Co3O4) catalyst designed to modulate adsorption sites.
Advantages: The oxygen vacancy (Vo) adsorbs OH- from the electrolyte, which then couples with HMF molecules, accelerating the rate-determining step and avoiding competitive adsorption of HMF and OH- on the same metal sites.
Catalysts: Anode: Vo-Co3O4

Paper Title: Tailoring Competitive Adsorption Sites by Oxygen-Vacancy on Cobalt Oxides to Enhance the Electrooxidation of Biomass
Key Feature: Pristine Co3O4 catalyst used as a baseline for comparison.
Limitations: Competitive adsorption between OH- and HMF molecules occurs on the limited reaction sites, leading to less efficient catalysis.
Catalysts: Anode: Co3O4

Paper Title: Toward selective electrooxidation of HMF to FDCA: Suppressing non-Faradaic transformations via low temperature electrolysis
Cell Type: H-cell separated by a Nafion membrane
Key Feature: Low-temperature (4°C) electrolysis is used to suppress the non-Faradaic degradation of HMF in a highly alkaline electrolyte.
Advantages: This strategy effectively suppresses spontaneous HMF degradation, reduces carbon loss to negligible levels (<1%), and enables high FDCA yield (~99%) and Faradaic efficiency (~97%) even at high HMF concentrations.
Limitations: The overall reaction rate is reduced at low temperature due to slower mass transfer of reactants from the bulk solution to the electrode surface.
Catalysts: Anode: Ni electrodeposited on carbon paper (Ni/CP) | Cathode: Pt foil

Paper Title: Trimetallic NiCoFe-Layered Double Hydroxides Nanosheets Efficient for Oxygen Evolution and Highly Selective Oxidation of Biomass-Derived 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
Key Feature: Trimetallic NiCoFe-layered double hydroxides (LDHs) ultrathin nanosheets (1.36 nm) grown on carbon fiber paper (CFP).
Advantages: Exhibited high performance in the oxidation of HMF to FDCA, requiring an ultralow overpotential, possessing excellent durability, and showing fast catalytic kinetics.
Catalysts: Anode: NiCoFe-LDHs/CFP, Cathode: Pt wire

Paper Title: Tuning the Selective Adsorption Site of Biomass on Co3O4 by Ir Single Atoms for Electrosynthesis
Key Feature: Single-atom Ir decorated on Co3O4 spinel oxide
Advantages: Enhanced HMF adsorption, faster reaction kinetics, optimal intermediate adsorption, and ultralow onset potential (1.15 V vs RHE).
Catalysts: Anode: Ir-Co3O4

Paper Title: Tuning the Selective Adsorption Site of Biomass on Co3O4 by Ir Single Atoms for Electrosynthesis
Key Feature: Bare Co3O4 spinel oxide (control catalyst)
Limitations: Higher onset potential (1.35 V vs RHE), lower yield, and lower Faradaic efficiency compared to Ir-Co3O4.
Catalysts: Anode: Co3O4

Paper Title: Two-dimensional metal-organic framework nanosheets for highly efficient electrocatalytic biomass 5-(hydroxymethyl)furfural (HMF) valorization
Key Feature: 2D Co-doped Ni-based Metal-Organic Framework (NiCoBDC) nanosheets grown directly on nickel foam substrate.
Advantages: Benefitting from the accessible pores for HMF molecules, abundant exposed active sites, and coupling effects between Ni and Co atoms, the catalyst realized a high catalytic activity and a robust electrochemical durability.
Limitations: The total FDCA yield rate decreased as the electrolysis continued, implying that a batch reactor is a limitation for industrialization compared to a flow reactor. MOF-based catalysts can also show modest stability in long-term electrolysis.
Catalysts: Anode: Co-doped 2D MOFs NiCoBDC on Nickel Foam (NiCoBDC-NF), Cathode: Pt plate

Paper Title: Ultrathin layered double hydroxides nanosheets array towards efficient electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural coupled with hydrogen generation
Key Feature: In-situ electrochemical exfoliation of CoAl-LDH to form ultrathin nanosheet arrays with abundant oxygen vacancies (E-CoAl-LDH-NSA).
Advantages: Achieves high faradaic efficiency (99.4% at 1.52 V vs. RHE), largely depresses the competing oxygen evolution reaction (OER), enhances exposure of reactive sites, and shows excellent robustness.
Catalysts: Working Electrode: E-CoAl-LDH-NSA on Ni foam

Paper Title: Ultrathin layered double hydroxides nanosheets array towards efficient electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural coupled with hydrogen generation
Key Feature: Coupling HMF oxidation with hydrogen (H2) production using the same catalyst (E-CoAl-LDH-NSA) for both anode and cathode.
Advantages: Low cell voltage (1.74 V to reach 50 mA/cm2), high H2 yield (44.16 L/h/m2), high FDCA yield (63.38 g/h/m2), and excellent stability with high Faradaic efficiencies for both products.
Catalysts: Anode: E-CoAl-LDH-NSA on Ni foam, Cathode: E-CoAl-LDH-NSA on Ni foam

Paper Title: Understanding the Roles of Electrogenerated Co3+ and Co4+ in Selectivity-Tuned 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Oxidation
Key Feature: Potential-tuned selectivity based on controlling the dominant Co oxidation state (Co3+ vs Co4+).
Advantages: Achieves high Faradaic efficiency and selectivity towards the fully oxidized product (FDCA) with significantly faster kinetics compared to lower potentials.
Limitations: At higher potentials (e.g., 1.5 V), the competing oxygen evolution reaction becomes more significant, reducing the Faradaic efficiency for HMF oxidation.
Catalysts: Anode: Electrodeposited CoOₓHᵧ on carbon cloth, Cathode: Not specified in paper

Paper Title: Unraveling the Electrocatalytic Activity in HMF Oxidation to FDCA by Fine-Tuning the Degree of NiOOH Phase Over Ni Nanoparticles Supported on Graphene Oxide
Key Feature: Electrochemical pre-treatment of a NiNPs/GO-Ni-foam catalyst to form a high-valence NiOOH active phase, which enhances HMF oxidation performance.
Advantages: Enhancing the portion of the NiOOH phase on the electrocatalyst surface improves electrocatalytic activity in terms of Faradaic efficiency and FDCA yield.
Limitations: Increasing the thickness of the NiOOH layer beyond an optimal point can negatively affect the electrochemical oxidation of HMF by increasing the work function of the working electrode.
Catalysts: Anode: Electrochemically treated 50-NiNPs/GO-Ni-foam | Cathode: Platinum gauze

Paper Title: Which electrode is better for biomass valorization: Cu(OH)2 or CuO nanowire?
Key Feature: Free-standing Cu(OH)2 nanowires grown directly on 3D copper foam (CuF) substrate.
Advantages: The method avoids sacrificial templates, prevents increased contact resistance, and enhances electrolyte diffusion.
Catalysts: Anode: Cu(OH)2 NWs/CuF, Cathode: Pt mesh

Paper Title: Which electrode is better for biomass valorization: Cu(OH)2 or CuO nanowire?
Key Feature: Free-standing CuO nanowires on 3D copper foam (CuF), prepared by calcination of Cu(OH)2 NWs.
Advantages: Three-fold enhanced number of Cu atoms on the surface, lower applied potential requirement, and increased electron transfer rate compared to Cu(OH)2 NWs.
Catalysts: Anode: CuO NWs/CuF, Cathode: Pt mesh
